title: Run one cross-account computer task end to end (F-computer)
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing — the customer account, role, and enabled org from `b88c0a` already exist
- **Unblocks:** honest pricing, the pitch page's central claim, and any customer onboarding

---

## This fell between two closed issues

`chatticus-061a11` ("The organization computer launches in the customer account") closed on its own DoD — *"the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason"* — which it met: launch account is always `organization.aws_account_id`, and a missing home or unreachable role refuses with zero Anthus RunTask. That is correct work.

But its closing comment says plainly: **"Live RunTask in a customer account still waits on `b88c0a`."**

`b88c0a` then closed on *"the timed runbook and person-steps"*, with **F-computer not attempted**. So the handoff was recorded on both sides and picked up by neither.

**The result: the behavior the whole epic exists for has never been executed once.** `061a11`'s own description calls it *"the behavior the whole epic exists for"* and *"the strongest thing on the pitch page."* What `b88c0a` proved was a **computerless** turn (`pong`). The cross-account compute path is specced, gated, and unrun.

## Why this goes before the self-setup stories

`9c8dbf`, `070cb4` and `7622fd` are **known** gaps — wiring UI and HTTP to kernel calls that already exist. They are buildable and their scope will not surprise anyone.

F-computer is **unknown**, and `b88c0a` recorded concrete reasons to expect it to fail:

- The published role CFN is scoped to `ChatticusComputers*` — **not `ChatticusSnapshots`**.
- ComputerWorker **does not deploy** a customer `ChatticusComputers` stack.
- There is **no ECS cluster or ECR `:dev` image** in the customer account. A Dynamo computer row exists; the compute infrastructure does not.

Any of those may require changing the published template. **By `chatticus-8a25af`'s own rule, a template change is customer-visible — an existing customer has to re-run it.** That makes this cheap to discover now and expensive to discover after the first customer onboards.

This is the same ordering that paid off in `chatticus-e9ddec`: measure the unknown before building the known.

## What to run

The `b88c0a` lab assets still exist — customer member account, `ChatticusCrossAccountRole`, enabled ACME org, AWS home written. Ids are in gitignored `AGENTS.local.md`.

Attempt one **computer-requiring** bot task in that account and follow it wherever it stops:

1. Does ComputerWorker assume the customer role and reach ECS at all?
2. What is missing in the customer account — cluster, task definition, ECR image, snapshot bucket, log group?
3. Which of those should the **published template** create, which should Chatticus deploy under the assumed role, and which are a separate customer-run stack?
4. Does the refuse-not-fallback guarantee from `061a11` hold live? **A silent fallback to the Anthus account is the failure that matters most** — it would work, look fine, and put customer workload and cost somewhere neither party agreed to.

## Record

Same discipline as `b88c0a`: placeholders in the wiki, real ids in `AGENTS.local.md`, every deviation labeled. Add the elapsed time to the provisioning runbook — the ~19 min figure currently excludes this entirely.

## Done when

One bot task requiring a computer has run in the customer account, **or** the exact missing infrastructure is documented with a decision on who creates it. A template change, if needed, is recorded as customer-visible on `chatticus-8a25af`.

comments.text:
Starting F-computer on the `b88c0a` lab assets (no seed). Composer 2.5 planning: worktree `/tmp/chatticus-2f2d87-f-computer` on `spike/2f2d87-f-computer`. Wiki on `develop` after the stop is labeled. Do not treat the ~19 min figure as including this.

**Snapshot decision (do not rediscover):** customer `/workspace` packs live in the **customer** account, not in Anthus `ChatticusSnapshots`. Pitch claim is that the file system rests in the account they own. Anthus `ChatticusSnapshots` stays for Anthus-managed orgs. F-computer must not grant or copy customer workplace bytes into the Anthus bucket. Template/stack work to create that customer bucket is customer-visible (`8a25af`); this card records the stop, it does not slip a template edit.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Plan reviewed. Worktree `/tmp/chatticus-2f2d87-f-computer` on `spike/2f2d87-f-computer` verified (not the primary clone). Authorizing the live attempt with one hole closed:

`POST .../turns/{id}/resume` **refuses** while the computer is stopped (`ComputerNotReadyError`). It cannot be the path that first summons ComputerWorker. After the UI turn is `waiting` on `workspace`, the labeled operator path is kernel `enqueue_computer_continuation` (does not require a running host). Record resume-won't-start-stopped-computer as a product gap. Do not treat a 409 from resume as F-computer done — that never reached AssumeRole.

Everything else in the plan stands: AWS-home gate first, dual-account ECS, zero Anthus RunTask, no template edit, no seed, no customer bytes in Anthus S3.

comments.text: Human UI: Ping answered **no** (computerless text, no `request_computer_capability`). That is `STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL` on the customer path — host start never ran. Taking the labeled kernel fallback (`prepare_computer_tool` + `enqueue_computer_continuation`) so F-computer still measures AssumeRole / missing `ChatticusComputers` / refuse-not-fallback.
